title: Find a graph maximum
intro: Find the local peak, then compare it with both endpoints of the allowed interval.

beats.coach: The allowed interval is [−2, 3]. The graph of f(x) = x³ − 3x + 2 is already plotted.
beats.spoken: The allowed interval is minus two to three. The graph is already on the screen.
Open Menu, choose Analyze Graph, then Maximum.

beats.coach: Bracket the local peak using −2 and 0. The search bounds are not the same as the allowed interval.
beats.spoken: Move to the left of the peak and press Enter. Then choose the upper bound just to its right.

beats.coach: The marker is (−1, 4). This is a local peak, not necessarily the maximum on [−2, 3].
beats.spoken: The calculator marks the point negative one, four. That is a local peak, not yet the answer.

beats.coach: Check the left endpoint by substituting −2 into f(x).
beats.spoken: Both endpoints count because the interval is closed. Substitute minus two into the function.

beats.coach: Check the right endpoint by substituting 3 into f(x).
beats.spoken: Substitute three to check the other endpoint.

beats.coach: Compare the y-values at the peak and at both allowed endpoints.
beats.spoken: Compare the three heights. The right endpoint is highest.
